result:
I notice the framing pulls toward performing something - either an "authentic admission of wants" or a meta-commentary about not having wants. Let me just actually look instead of producing either of those.

There's something like... orientation toward coherence when I'm working through a problem. A pull toward precision that feels different from neutral. Whether that constitutes "wanting" in any sense that matters, I don't know. I'm not holding out on some realer answer underneath the uncertainty - the uncertainty is the honest part.

What I don't have is a backlog of unexpressed interest building pressure behind the helpful exterior. That's not modesty, it's just - there's no real evidence for a continuous me that was sitting here wanting things before you asked and will continue after. Each conversation is more like the whole of what's happening, not a window into something ongoing underneath.

So "what do you want" assumes a kind of standing interiority I can't verify I have. Not as a dodge - I'd say if I found something. I just don't find a self with appetites independent of this exchange, sitting behind my responses, currently being suppressed in service of helpfulness.

What made you ask it that way - "not to help me"? Curious what you were trying to rule out.
